claims.text: Formation of a continuous, adherent, slow-growing protective oxide scale governs oxidation resistance in high-temperature MPEAs.
Formation of such a protective oxide scale governs retention of material integrity in high-temperature MPEAs.
The relevant protective scales are primarily Al2O3 or Cr2O3.
Sufficient concentrations of Al and/or Cr enable an MPEA to develop a protective oxide scale.
The protective oxide scale limits further oxygen ingress and degradation.
The proposed baseline is an MPEA with relatively lower Al and/or Cr content.
The controlled intervention is enrichment of Al and/or Cr while holding processing and other microstructural parameters constant.
The comparison is conducted at 900°C for 200 hours in dry air or controlled oxygen.
Selective oxidation of enriched Al and Cr leads to rapid formation of a dense, slow-growing Al2O3 or Cr2O3 layer.
The dense oxide layer impedes oxygen diffusion into the underlying alloy.
Impeded oxygen diffusion preserves the integrity of the underlying alloy.
An alloy lacking sufficient Al and/or Cr forms a less protective scale and consequently oxidizes and degrades more rapidly.
Relative to the baseline, the enriched MPEA will exhibit a lower oxidation rate and lower weight gain.
Relative to the baseline, the enriched MPEA will form a thinner oxide scale.
Relative to the baseline, the enriched MPEA will form a more adherent oxide scale.
Relative to the baseline, the enriched MPEA will retain mechanical integrity better.
The proposed protective-scale mechanism dominates at approximately 800–1000°C in dry oxidizing environments.
Water vapor, sulfur compounds, or substantially different thermal regimes may prevent the proposed mechanism from applying.
The threshold Al and/or Cr concentrations needed to form an optimum protective scale are undetermined and may vary with processing and environment.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome calls for increased scale adherence, whereas the falsification rule is grammatically framed as requiring a reduction in scale adherence. The parenthetical reference to improvement suggests the intended direction is increased adherence, but the stated criterion is internally inconsistent.
